pathway.title: ATS Corp /ATS — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. Leverage is above target and rising (Documentary Fact). Net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA was 3.1x at September 27, 2026 against 2.8x at March 31, 2026 and 3.0x at December 28, 2025, with the company's own range at 2.0x to 3.0x [financial base, leverage chart and finding on leverage]. Net debt rose by C$ 41.0 million to C$ 1,192.2 million while trailing EBITDA fell by C$ 31.7 million, partly because ATS spent C$ 61.3 million on share repurchases; excluding them management puts leverage at 3.0x. Management expects to stay moderately above the range for the rest of FY2027 [business context, leverage expectation conflict]. On the same figures, net debt of C$ 48.3 million less, or EBITDA of C$ 16.1 million more, would return leverage to 3.0x (calculated here, see Calculations). The pending C$ 71.2 million sale of two U.S. facilities is earmarked by management for restructuring costs, so it should not be assumed to reduce net debt.

2. Liquidity is strong and the maturity wall is distant (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on the risk). ATS holds C$ 231.0 million of cash and C$ 966.7 million of unutilized credit, giving C$ 1,197.7 million. The secured revolver of C$ 900.0 million matures December 4, 2029, and letters of credit of about C$ 274.4 million sit on separate facilities and do not reduce it [financial base, liquidity build]. The first large principal maturity on disclosed instruments is the US$ 350.0 million 4.125% senior notes in December 2028, hedged only in part and only to December 2027, followed by the C$ 600.0 million 6.50% notes in August 2032. Refinancing risk is therefore concentrated in the FY2029 notes and the FY2030 credit facility expiry rather than in the next twelve months.

3. Earnings are falling on volume and mix (Documentary Fact). Six month revenues fell 7.2% and Q2 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.1% against 14.2%, while Order Bookings rose 12.7% to C$ 827 million [financial base; business context operating model]. The backlog of C$ 2,009 million is 2.9% lower than a year earlier, with industrial and consumer backlog at C$ 312 million against C$ 431 million. Management no longer expects its prior FY2027 revenue growth and margin goals and guides Q3 FY2027 revenue to C$ 640 million to C$ 680 million. The risk mechanic is operating leverage: a fixed cost base on lower volumes compresses margins faster than revenue, which lowers the EBITDA that covenants and leverage ratios are measured on.

4. Adjusted EBITDA flatters earning power (Analyst Interpretation on documentary add-back data). The net add-back from EBITDA to adjusted EBITDA was C$ 20.2 million in Q2 FY2027, 25.0% of adjusted EBITDA, and restructuring charges have been added back in FY2025, FY2026 and the first half of FY2027 [financial base, add-back review]. The credit agreement definition of EBITDA is not available, so covenant EBITDA may be higher or lower. Creditors should treat the C$ 381.3 million as an upper bound for recurring earnings until restructuring stops recurring.

5. Cash flow is dominated by working capital timing (Documentary Fact). FY2026 operating cash flow of C$ 448.4 million included a C$ 246.6 million working capital release, 55.0% of the total; six month FY2027 operating cash flow was C$ 70.3 million and free cash flow C$ 36.5 million against C$ 149.6 million a year earlier, when an EV customer settlement was collected [financial base, cash flow quality]. Debt reduction capacity therefore moves with project billing, and restructuring provisions point to cash costs still to come.

6. Cover is adequate today (Documentary Fact with calculation). Trailing EBITDA to cash interest paid is 4.18x against 4.24x for FY2026, helped by lower debt and net finance costs of C$ 42.9 million for six months against C$ 50.0 million. A forward swap fixes the term loan at 3.264% from November 4, 2026; floating exposure on the revolver and the end of the cross-currency hedge in December 2027 are sensitivities [financial base, instruments].

7. Business risk is moderate and visibility is reasonable but not strong (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Four end markets, three regions and a backlog of C$ 2,009 million support revenue visibility, and management targets recurring revenue of 25% to 35% of trailing revenue, a figure not yet reported and so treated as Management Language [business context, operating model]. Offsetting this, project timing is lumpy, tariffs under Section 338 delayed non-life-sciences orders from late August 2026 (partly eased by late October modifications), and cross-border equipment sales into the U.S. were just over 20% of FY2026 adjusted revenues.

8. Governance signals are mixed (Analyst Interpretation). ATS reduced net debt between March 2025 and March 2026, a supportive record, but repurchased shares at above-target leverage, changed CEO and has had an interim CFO since February 2026 [business context, governance table]. Disclosure controls were not effective at September 27, 2026 because of a material weakness, so every reported figure carries added reliability risk. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed and no creditor-adverse action is described in the sources reviewed, which is a statement about the pack rather than proof.

Liquidity depth (Documentary Fact): C$ 231.0 million cash plus C$ 966.7 million unutilized credit against a modest near-term maturity profile, with the revolver expiring in December 2029. Backlog and recurring revenue ambition (Documentary Fact and Management Language): C$ 2,009 million of backlog supports near-term revenue, and services growth is a stabilizer. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact): net debt to EBITDA fell from 3.9x at March 31, 2025 to 2.8x at March 31, 2026 before the recent reversal. Interest cover (Documentary Fact with calculation): 4.18x on trailing cash interest. Restructuring programme (Management Language, qualified): management targets C$ 65 million to C$ 75 million of annualized savings, which is a claim and not yet a result.

Weaknesses. Leverage above target (Documentary Fact): 3.1x against 2.0x to 3.0x, with management expecting to remain above range through FY2027. Falling earnings (Documentary Fact): trailing pro forma adjusted EBITDA C$ 381.3 million down from C$ 413.0 million, and revenue and margin goals withdrawn. Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation): recurring restructuring add-backs of C$ 20.2 million in the latest quarter. Cash flow volatility (Documentary Fact): FY2026 relied on a C$ 246.6 million working capital release. Capital allocation (Analyst Interpretation): C$ 61.3 million of buybacks while leverage was above range. Control environment (Documentary Fact): material weakness and ineffective disclosure controls, with a new CEO and an interim CFO. Missing structure (Insufficient Information): no covenant levels, no credit agreement or indentures, no guarantor names, no customer concentration figures and no ownership detail, so covenant headroom, priority of claims and single-customer risk cannot be assessed.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no leveraged buyout, merger, sponsor transaction or acquisition financing in the pack, and the context carries no deal terms. The sources describe corporate actions rather than a single transaction. On debt, the company amended its senior secured credit facility on December 4, 2025, extending maturity to December 4, 2029, with a revolving line of 900.0 and a fully drawn term facility of 150.0, and it incurred transaction costs of 2.6; the facility was utilized at 190.0 at September 27, 2026. The Canadian dollar senior notes of 600.0 at 6.50 percent due August 21, 2032 were placed in two tranches in August and December 2024, and the U.S. dollar senior notes of US$350.0 at 4.125 percent are due December 15, 2028. Neither note series was issued in the period covered by the current or prior fiscal year, and no new debt issue is disclosed in FY2026 or the first half of FY2027 other than draws of 85.0 in FY2026 and 40.0 in Q2 FY2027 reported as proceeds from long-term debt (financial base module). On equity, the company announced a normal course issuer bid in December 2025 allowing purchase of up to 8,225,621 shares, and bought 2,244,461 shares for 61.3 in Q2 FY2027. On assets, two U.S. facilities and one German facility are held for sale as part of the transportation reorganization; after quarter end the company completed the sale of the two U.S. facilities for 71.2 with an estimated gain of about 12.2, with one leased back, to be recognized in Q3 FY2027, and the proceeds are expected to fund restructuring. On operations, the Fixed Cost Transformation Program was announced with Q1 FY2027 results on August 6, 2026. The earlier business acquisitions in FY2025, the companies Heidolph and Paxiom, are named as contributors to growth, but their dates, prices and financing are not in the pack. The legal terms of the notes and credit facility, such as covenant levels and baskets that would govern capacity for dividends, debt incurrence or asset disposals, are described only in general terms because the executed documents are absent.

fields.value: ATS Corporation entered Q2 FY2027 with a moderately levered balance sheet that is drifting the wrong way. The company's own measure, net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA, rose from 2.8x at March 31, 2026 to 3.1x at September 27, 2026, because trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA fell while net debt rose, helped along by a share repurchase of 61.3 under the normal course issuer bid. Management now expects to operate above its 2.0x to 3.0x target range for the rest of FY2027. Earnings pressure is volume driven: six month FY2027 revenues fell 7.2% year over year (1,359.5 against 1,465.2) and Q2 FY2027 revenues fell while Order Bookings rose, so backlog of 2,009 supports near-term revenue but at a lower margin. Debt service looks comfortable on cash interest cover of 4.18x for the trailing twelve months, and liquidity is large relative to the debt wall: the senior secured revolver runs to December 2029, and the first large principal maturity on the disclosed instruments is the U.S. dollar senior notes in December 2028. The quality of the numbers deserves care. Cash flow in FY2026 was flattered by a large working capital release, adjusted EBITDA adds back restructuring charges that recur every year, the covenant tests are described but not quantified, the interim statements arrive without notes, and management reports a material weakness in internal control. The view is therefore moderate leverage, strong liquidity, deteriorating earnings and incomplete covenant evidence.

fields.value: Operating cash flow is dominated by working capital timing. FY2026 operating cash flow of 448.4 included a change in non-cash operating working capital of 246.6, which is 55.0% of the total (C6). Six months FY2026 operating cash flow also benefited from a customer settlement: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:24] "collection of the settlement amount with an electric vehicle". Cash interest paid was close to net finance costs (43.3 against 42.9 for six months FY2027), and the share repurchase of 61.3 in Q2 FY2027 consumed more than the entire six month free cash flow. Capital expenditure guidance for FY2027 is 60 to 80 ([6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:25] "between $60 million and $80 million"). fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ATS is a long-established, publicly listed Canadian builder of automated manufacturing and assembly systems, with products and services spread over four end markets and a global footprint. For a creditor the central business facts are visibility and cyclicality. Order Backlog of 2,009 at September 27, 2026 and a recurring revenue share that management expects at 25 to 35 percent of trailing twelve month revenue give some protection, but customer capital decisions, the timing of large life sciences programs, tariffs and a fall in revenue have moved earnings down, while management has said it will not meet its prior FY2027 growth and margin goals. The company is in the middle of a restructuring: a transportation reorganization that is repositioning a former end market, a services reorganization, and a multi-phase Fixed Cost Transformation Program with facility closures and a workforce reduction of 300 to 400. These actions are meant to lift margins toward a 15 percent long-term target but cost cash first. There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor or acquisition financing in the sources: the debt arose from earlier note issues and a revolving credit facility amended in December 2025, and the only transaction events in the period are facility sales, share repurchases and restructuring. Ownership is dispersed public equity as far as the pack shows, though the annual information form that would confirm holders is missing. Governance signals are mixed: a new CEO and an interim CFO, a reported material weakness in internal controls, and share buybacks while leverage is above target, set against deleveraging during FY2026. Customer concentration is named as a risk factor but never quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no leveraged buyout, merger, sponsor transaction or acquisition financing in the pack, and the context carries no deal terms. The sources describe corporate actions rather than a single transaction. On debt, the company amended its senior secured credit facility on December 4, 2025, extending maturity to December 4, 2029, with a revolving line of 900.0 and a fully drawn term facility of 150.0, and it incurred transaction costs of 2.6; the facility was utilized at 190.0 at September 27, 2026. The Canadian dollar senior notes of 600.0 at 6.50 percent due August 21, 2032 were placed in two tranches in August and December 2024, and the U.S. dollar senior notes of US$350.0 at 4.125 percent are due December 15, 2028. Neither note series was issued in the period covered by the current or prior fiscal year, and no new debt issue is disclosed in FY2026 or the first half of FY2027 other than draws of 85.0 in FY2026 and 40.0 in Q2 FY2027 reported as proceeds from long-term debt (financial base module). On equity, the company announced a normal course issuer bid in December 2025 allowing purchase of up to 8,225,621 shares, and bought 2,244,461 shares for 61.3 in Q2 FY2027. On assets, two U.S. facilities and one German facility are held for sale as part of the transportation reorganization; after quarter end the company completed the sale of the two U.S. facilities for 71.2 with an estimated gain of about 12.2, with one leased back, to be recognized in Q3 FY2027, and the proceeds are expected to fund restructuring. On operations, the Fixed Cost Transformation Program was announced with Q1 FY2027 results on August 6, 2026. The earlier business acquisitions in FY2025, the companies Heidolph and Paxiom, are named as contributors to growth, but their dates, prices and financing are not in the pack. The legal terms of the notes and credit facility, such as covenant levels and baskets that would govern capacity for dividends, debt incurrence or asset disposals, are described only in general terms because the executed documents are absent.

fields.value: ATS Corporation is a moderately leveraged, well-funded industrial automation supplier whose earnings are weakening and whose leverage has moved above its own target. The strongest support is liquidity: C$ 231.0 million of cash and C$ 966.7 million of unutilized credit, a revolver running to December 2029, and a first large principal maturity only in December 2028, alongside four end markets and a C$ 2,009 million backlog. The weakest point is the trend: trailing pro forma adjusted EBITDA of C$ 381.3 million is down from C$ 413.0 million, net debt to EBITDA is 3.1x against a 2.0x to 3.0x target, and cash generation is lumpy. The outcome turns on whether the Fixed Cost Transformation Program savings arrive and backlog converts before further buybacks or working capital absorb cash, and on covenant terms nobody outside the company can see in this pack.

fields.value: Thesis: ATS Corporation can service and refinance its debt from a large liquidity cushion and a diversified backlog, but its credit quality depends on stabilizing earnings and returning leverage to range, which the current evidence does not yet show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Leverage is above target and rising (Documentary Fact). Net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA was 3.1x at September 27, 2026 against 2.8x at March 31, 2026 and 3.0x at December 28, 2025, with the company's own range at 2.0x to 3.0x [financial base, leverage chart and finding on leverage]. Net debt rose by C$ 41.0 million to C$ 1,192.2 million while trailing EBITDA fell by C$ 31.7 million, partly because ATS spent C$ 61.3 million on share repurchases; excluding them management puts leverage at 3.0x. Management expects to stay moderately above the range for the rest of FY2027 [business context, leverage expectation conflict]. On the same figures, net debt of C$ 48.3 million less, or EBITDA of C$ 16.1 million more, would return leverage to 3.0x (calculated here, see Calculations). The pending C$ 71.2 million sale of two U.S. facilities is earmarked by management for restructuring costs, so it should not be assumed to reduce net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Liquidity is strong and the maturity wall is distant (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on the risk). ATS holds C$ 231.0 million of cash and C$ 966.7 million of unutilized credit, giving C$ 1,197.7 million. The secured revolver of C$ 900.0 million matures December 4, 2029, and letters of credit of about C$ 274.4 million sit on separate facilities and do not reduce it [financial base, liquidity build]. The first large principal maturity on disclosed instruments is the US$ 350.0 million 4.125% senior notes in December 2028, hedged only in part and only to December 2027, followed by the C$ 600.0 million 6.50% notes in August 2032. Refinancing risk is therefore concentrated in the FY2029 notes and the FY2030 credit facility expiry rather than in the next twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Earnings are falling on volume and mix (Documentary Fact). Six month revenues fell 7.2% and Q2 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.1% against 14.2%, while Order Bookings rose 12.7% to C$ 827 million [financial base; business context operating model]. The backlog of C$ 2,009 million is 2.9% lower than a year earlier, with industrial and consumer backlog at C$ 312 million against C$ 431 million. Management no longer expects its prior FY2027 revenue growth and margin goals and guides Q3 FY2027 revenue to C$ 640 million to C$ 680 million. The risk mechanic is operating leverage: a fixed cost base on lower volumes compresses margins faster than revenue, which lowers the EBITDA that covenants and leverage ratios are measured on.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Adjusted EBITDA flatters earning power (Analyst Interpretation on documentary add-back data). The net add-back from EBITDA to adjusted EBITDA was C$ 20.2 million in Q2 FY2027, 25.0% of adjusted EBITDA, and restructuring charges have been added back in FY2025, FY2026 and the first half of FY2027 [financial base, add-back review]. The credit agreement definition of EBITDA is not available, so covenant EBITDA may be higher or lower. Creditors should treat the C$ 381.3 million as an upper bound for recurring earnings until restructuring stops recurring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Cash flow is dominated by working capital timing (Documentary Fact). FY2026 operating cash flow of C$ 448.4 million included a C$ 246.6 million working capital release, 55.0% of the total; six month FY2027 operating cash flow was C$ 70.3 million and free cash flow C$ 36.5 million against C$ 149.6 million a year earlier, when an EV customer settlement was collected [financial base, cash flow quality]. Debt reduction capacity therefore moves with project billing, and restructuring provisions point to cash costs still to come.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Cover is adequate today (Documentary Fact with calculation). Trailing EBITDA to cash interest paid is 4.18x against 4.24x for FY2026, helped by lower debt and net finance costs of C$ 42.9 million for six months against C$ 50.0 million. A forward swap fixes the term loan at 3.264% from November 4, 2026; floating exposure on the revolver and the end of the cross-currency hedge in December 2027 are sensitivities [financial base, instruments].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Business risk is moderate and visibility is reasonable but not strong (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Four end markets, three regions and a backlog of C$ 2,009 million support revenue visibility, and management targets recurring revenue of 25% to 35% of trailing revenue, a figure not yet reported and so treated as Management Language [business context, operating model]. Offsetting this, project timing is lumpy, tariffs under Section 338 delayed non-life-sciences orders from late August 2026 (partly eased by late October modifications), and cross-border equipment sales into the U.S. were just over 20% of FY2026 adjusted revenues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Governance signals are mixed (Analyst Interpretation). ATS reduced net debt between March 2025 and March 2026, a supportive record, but repurchased shares at above-target leverage, changed CEO and has had an interim CFO since February 2026 [business context, governance table]. Disclosure controls were not effective at September 27, 2026 because of a material weakness, so every reported figure carries added reliability risk. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed and no creditor-adverse action is described in the sources reviewed, which is a statement about the pack rather than proof.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Liquidity depth (Documentary Fact): C$ 231.0 million cash plus C$ 966.7 million unutilized credit against a modest near-term maturity profile, with the revolver expiring in December 2029. Diversification (Documentary Fact): four end markets and three regions, with life sciences holding the largest backlog at C$ 1,238 million. Backlog and recurring revenue ambition (Documentary Fact and Management Language): C$ 2,009 million of backlog supports near-term revenue, and services growth is a stabilizer. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact): net debt to EBITDA fell from 3.9x at March 31, 2025 to 2.8x at March 31, 2026 before the recent reversal. Interest cover (Documentary Fact with calculation): 4.18x on trailing cash interest. Restructuring programme (Management Language, qualified): management targets C$ 65 million to C$ 75 million of annualized savings, which is a claim and not yet a result.

fields.name: Quote

Nearly every figure in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis traces to a located page in the pinned filings, and recalculation reproduced all leverage and cover figures from separately extracted filing lines, plus the liquidity and add-back arithmetic from inputs checked against the pages. The most important provenance gap is covenant compliance: the credit agreement is absent, so statements that covenants were met are management assertions that cannot be tested. A second gap is that audited annual statements and notes are missing, so FY2026 figures rest on the year-end release. Only minor defects were found, none of which changes the credit view. Because the same analyst wrote the modules and this trace, an independent second reviewer should repeat the highest-risk checks before the report is used.
